findings.title: canManage() grants manage rights to admins holding only the view scope on all groups
findings.body: In GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() the fallback permission check is `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`, i.e. it returns true when the caller has either the VIEW or the MANAGE scope on the all-groups resource. This appears to be a copy-paste of canView() directly above it. As a result, an admin who is granted only a 'view' permission for all groups (e.g. via an all-groups scope permission with the view scope) is treated as being able to manage groups globally: the no-arg canManage()/requireManage() is what GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup() uses to authorize creating top-level groups, so a view-only admin can create groups. Per-group manage (canManage(GroupModel)) correctly checks only MANAGE, so the no-arg variant should drop AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW from the expected scopes.

findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns authz resource IDs instead of group IDs
findings.body: In GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission(), the granted set is populated with `groupResource.getId()`, which is the authorization-store Resource UUID. In the V2 schema the group ID is stored as the resource *name* (AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup returns group.getId() and getOrCreateResource creates the resource with that name). Callers of this method — UsersResource.searchForUser, BruteForceUsersResource.searchForUser and UsersResource.getUsersCount — feed the returned IDs into the UserModel.GROUPS session attribute / group-filtered count queries, which expect real group IDs. Concretely: an admin whose only user visibility comes from a view-members/manage-members permission on all groups will get a non-empty set containing a resource UUID, the GROUPS session attribute is set with it, and searchForUserStream filters by membership in a non-existent group, so the admin sees zero users. The method should add groupResource.getName() (the group ID), mirroring what the V1 implementation did by stripping the prefix from the resource name.

findings.title: Per-resource permission check in getGroupIdsWithViewPermission looks up resources by ID as if it were a name, and per-group resources are never typed
findings.body: Inside the findByType visitor in GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission(), the code calls `hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), VIEW_MEMBERS, MANAGE_MEMBERS)`. However hasPermission(String groupId, ...) does `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)`, so it is passed a resource ID where a resource name is expected; the lookup returns null and evaluation silently falls back to the all-groups resource instead of evaluating the policies attached to that specific group resource. Additionally, resources created by AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource never have their type set (no setType call), so resourceStore.findByType(server, GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...) will not even iterate per-group resources — only the 'all groups' resource created in init() carries the type. Net effect: view-members/manage-members grants on individual groups are never detected by this method, and (combined with the getId() bug) the group-ID set used to filter user searches is wrong or empty.

findings.title: No upgrade path for realms that enabled admin permissions before the Groups resource type existed
findings.body: AdminPermissionsSchema.init() creates the 'Groups' all-resource and the group-specific scopes (manage-members, view-members, manage-membership) only when the admin-permissions client is first created for a realm. Realms that already have admin permissions enabled (resource server initialized by an earlier version) will never get the new resource type or scopes, and this PR adds no migration. Consequences for such realms: AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceTypeResource() returns null for 'Groups', and GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission then calls `policyStore.findByResource(server, null)`, which dereferences the null resource in the JPA store implementation and throws (500 on group admin endpoints); likewise creating any group permission fails because the scope lookups in getOrCreateResource find no 'manage-members'/'view-members' scopes and throw ModelException("No scopes found."). A migration/initialization step that adds the new resource type and scopes to existing admin-permissions resource servers is needed.

findings.title: getResourceName does not resolve names for the new Groups resource type
findings.body: AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceName() resolves human-readable names only for the Users resource type; for everything else it returns resource.getDisplayName(). Group resources created via getOrCreateResource are named by group ID and never have a display name set, so anywhere this method is used to present resources of a Groups-type policy (e.g. permission listings in the admin UI), the entry will show null/empty instead of the group's name or path. A GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE branch resolving the group (e.g. its name or path) should be added, analogous to the existing Users handling.
